A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Triple Preference Optimization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, replaced, and newly added content to be distinguished.

before.justification: v1 reports original Phi-2 and Mistral alignment experiments, benchmark results, and hyperparameter and SFT ablations in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 reports original TPO/TPO-L experiments, robustness and reward analyses, and a human assessment of automated judges. These qualify independently of baseline scores explicitly borrowed from prior work.

M1.justification: The original TPO objective remains in Equation 10, but v2 introduces TPO-L in Equation 11. This variant length-normalizes preferred and rejected response log probabilities and introduces a reward margin gamma, substantively extending the optimization method.

E1.justification: v2 adds GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, Arena-Hard, and MixEval-Hard, extending mathematical reasoning, harder knowledge questions, and conversational evaluation. It also uses newly generated response pools ranked by ArmoRM and PairRM. MT-Bench and the earlier leaderboard tasks remain, but BB-causal, BB-sports, BB-formal, and OpenBookQA evaluations disappear.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated SimPO and SLiC-HF baselines alongside the retained SFT, DPO, IPO, KTO, CPO, and ORPO comparisons (Tables 2–3 and 11–12). SimPO becomes a central comparator for the method's reward and length-control claims. SLiC-HF was discussed in v1 but had no reported comparison results.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the Phi-2/Mistral-v0.1 configurations with Llama-3-8B and newer Mistral configurations. Its Base experiments use a score-gap-filtered UltraFeedback pool and 5K/10K/20K/40K subsets, replacing predominantly 10K preference training; Instruct experiments use 60K datasets. Reported schedules and batches also change. New protocols include DAA, GPT-4o judging for Arena-Hard, and a 100-sample assessment by three human judges.

E4.justification: v2 adds preference-label reversal with clean gold responses, equal-score gold/preferred responses, response-rank selection, reward-distribution and margin analyses, verbosity checks, judge validation, and chat-template and microbatch studies. Data-size and stronger-SFT controls substantially extend the earlier analyses. The standalone SFT-skipping and epoch/learning-rate result tables from v1 are not retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's reward histograms and per-annotator judgment error rates describe outcomes rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The earlier Phi-2 and Mistral-v0.1 result sets are replaced by extensive results under new configurations. For example, v2 Table 2 reports 5K Base GSM8K accuracy of 51.9 for TPO versus 32.9 for DPO, and 40K Arena-Hard scores of 12.3 for TPO-L versus 5.3 for DPO. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The optimal-policy derivation, gradient, reward-equivalence proofs, and Pareto argument are largely retained in v2 Appendix B. However, Equation 3 changes distribution entropy to mean token negative log likelihood without carrying the normalization into Equation 4. The newly defined TPO-L loss also prints a gold-response term whose sign conflicts with the stated behavioral-cloning objective.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes single-step alignment with less data and improved benchmark performance. v2 retains that claim but makes simultaneous reasoning and instruction-following improvement central, introduces TPO-L as a contribution, and adds headline claims about verbosity control, judgment-noise robustness, dataset-size stability, and superior implicit reward modeling.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations linking noise resistance to the clean gold-response objective and reduced verbosity to behavioral cloning rather than shorter training responses. It develops the CPO optimization-conflict interpretation and discusses reward-margin tradeoffs across tasks. Appendix A adds limitations concerning margin tuning, qualifying-data scarcity, reasoning-specific training, and offline learning.

D1.justification: v2 supplies model/dataset identifiers, hyperparameter search ranges, per-setting alpha/beta/gamma values, sequence limits, accumulation configurations, and an expanded code-and-model access statement. Hardware reporting changes from four to eight A100 GPUs. However, v1's explicit optimizer, precision, epoch-count, and runtime disclosures disappear, and v2 Appendix C's batch-size prose conflicts with Table 6.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around SimPO, verbosity, reward modeling, automated judges, and offline versus iterative preference optimization. Section 5 adds numerous relevant works and explicitly situates TPO within offline learning. The relationship to SimPO now motivates TPO-L and several central comparative claims, exceeding a routine bibliography update.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around reasoning, robustness, and verbosity. Related work moves after the experiments; the earlier theory subsection and limitations move into appendices. A new challenges subsection and separate setup/results organization substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, redraws the method overview, and adds a dataset-construction diagram. It introduces extensive multi-panel reward, noise, and length plots, hyperparameter heatmaps, and reorganized result tables grouped by training size and initialization. These are substantive display changes beyond renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the retained TPO method's empirical support through shared-data size sweeps, stronger-SFT controls, noise and verbosity analyses, and human checks of the evaluator (Tables 2 and 5, Figures 4 and 9, Appendix F). These address important limits of v1's predominantly 10K study. The net gain is tempered by new inconsistencies in the entropy derivation and TPO-L loss, conflicting batch-size documentation, and lost training details. The expanded evidence is useful, but these defects limit mathematical clarity and reproducibility.
